advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wire reconcile_recovery's 'resume' disposition into run_loop: load the WipChain into state['wip'] to resume drive, and clear recovery.json once resolved.
evidence: infra/autolander/loop.py:523: `    reconcile_recovery(gerrit, root)` — return value discarded
infra/autolander/loop.py:525: `    state = {"wip": None, "phase_since": time.monotonic()}`
infra/autolander/loop.py:497: `    return "resume in-flight stack"` — resume branch does not unlink recovery.json nor is it acted on by the caller
Ticket AC: 'On restart the bot reads recovery.json + reconciles ... BEFORE selecting new work ... not merged? re-drive'
advisory.finding: reconcile_recovery returns 'resume in-flight stack' but run_loop ignores the return value and never loads recovery.json into state['wip']; the loop starts with state={'wip': None} and immediately re-selects from scratch. A stack that was genuinely mid-flight (tip not merged, SHA unchanged) is neither resumed nor cleared, and recovery.json is left on disk stale, so it will re-reconcile on every subsequent restart.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend recovery to persist the handback `acknowledged` flag and reconcile mid-handback stacks against the S3 MarkerStore (reconcile_on_restart) on restart.
evidence: infra/autolander/loop.py:456-462: snapshot has change_id/chain_member_ids/tested_shas/phase/re_drive_count — no `acknowledged` flag
infra/autolander/loop.py:481-497: reconcile_recovery consults only client.get_change; no MarkerStore / reconcile_on_restart usage
Ticket AC: 'a mid-handback stack completes the idempotent Autosubmit-removal (keyed by S3's acknowledged=false)' and recovery record must include 'the handback acknowledged flag'
infra/autolander/failure.py:186: `def reconcile_on_restart(client, store)` exists for exactly this
advisory.finding: reconcile_recovery only reconciles against live Gerrit for the tip change and does not reconcile against S3's MarkerStore, nor does write_recovery persist the `acknowledged` handback flag — so a bot killed mid-handback never completes the idempotent Autosubmit-removal on restart, which the ticket AC explicitly requires.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile SHA/submittable drift across every chain_member_id, not just the tip, in reconcile_recovery.
evidence: infra/autolander/loop.py:490: `    tip = client.get_change(wip.change_id, ["CURRENT_REVISION"])`
infra/autolander/loop.py:494: compares only `wip.tested_shas.get(wip.change_id)`
infra/autolander/loop.py:167: `chain_member_ids: list[str]  # all members bottom->top` — the snapshot records per-member tested_shas but reconcile ignores them
is_landable (loop.py:181) iterates every member — reconcile does not, an inconsistency in drift detection
advisory.finding: reconcile_recovery checks only the tip change (wip.change_id) for MERGED status and SHA drift, but a chain has multiple members (chain_member_ids); a non-tip member that drifted or failed to merge is not detected, so 'resume' can be returned for a stack that is actually inconsistent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the AUTOLANDER_ERROR emission stream: emit_marker and emit_autolander_error must target the same stdout/stderr contract observability.sh greps.
evidence: infra/autolander/loop.py:414: `    sys.stdout.write(token + " " + json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True) + "\n")`
infra/autolander/loop.py:283: `    sys.stderr.write(f"{AUTOLANDER_ERROR} {detail}\n")`
infra/autolander/loop.py:265-267: 'S5c's observability keys its ... alarm off this token on the container's stderr'
infra/autolander/loop.py:406-407: 'a single stdout line ... observability.sh greps'
infra/autolander/loop.py:412-414: emit_marker has no sys.stdout.flush()
infra/autolander/loop.py:284: emit_autolander_error DOES call `sys.stderr.flush()` — inconsistent
advisory.finding: The AUTOLANDER_ERROR marker is emitted on two different streams: emit_marker writes it to stdout, while the existing emit_autolander_error writes the identical token to stderr. The comment claims observability greps stderr in one place and stdout in another; a grep bound to one stream will miss errors emitted on the other.
merged_from: emit_marker writes to stdout without flushing; in a long-running containerized process stdout is typically block-buffered when not a TTY, so marker lines (the observability contract) may be delayed or lost on crash.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Collapse MARKER_ERROR and AUTOLANDER_ERROR into a single shared constant.
evidence: infra/autolander/loop.py:408: `MARKER_ERROR = "AUTOLANDER_ERROR"`
infra/autolander/loop.py:267: `AUTOLANDER_ERROR = "AUTOLANDER_ERROR"`
advisory.finding: MARKER_ERROR duplicates the pre-existing module constant AUTOLANDER_ERROR (both = 'AUTOLANDER_ERROR'); two names for the same token invite drift if one is changed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a reconcile_recovery test for the resume branch: NEW tip with current_revision == recorded tested SHA -> asserts the resume disposition AND that recovery.json is preserved.
evidence: infra/autolander/loop.py:497: `    return "resume in-flight stack"`
test_crash_recovery.py asserts only `"merged" in disposition` and `not (tmp_path / RECOVERY_FILE).exists()` (merged branch) and `"merged" not in disposition` + file gone (drift branch)

ABSENCE: no test constructs a NEW tip whose current_revision equals wip.tested_shas[change_id], calls reconcile_recovery, and asserts the disposition is the resume string and that RECOVERY_FILE STILL exists
infra/autolander/loop.py:482-484 docstring: `if a tested SHA no longer matches / not submittable → discard and re-select`
infra/autolander/loop.py:494: `if tip.get("current_revision") != wip.tested_shas.get(wip.change_id):` — the only discard condition; submittable is not consulted
ABSENCE: no test seeds a change_info(submittable=False) with a matching revision and asserts reconcile's disposition
advisory.finding: reconcile_recovery's third documented disposition — the 'resume in-flight stack' path (tip still NEW and recorded tested SHA still matches the live current_revision) — has no test. Both reconcile tests cover only the merged-clears and sha-drift-discards branches and each asserts recovery.json is REMOVED; nothing asserts the resume branch returns the resume disposition AND leaves recovery.json intact. A regression that discarded/cleared recovery on the resume path (stranding an in-flight stack) would not be caught.
merged_from: reconcile_recovery's docstring states a snapshot is discarded when the tip is 'not submittable', but no test exercises the submittability dimension of reconcile — every reconcile test drives discard via SHA mismatch only. A change whose current_revision still matches the recorded tested SHA but is no longer submittable is untested (and in fact would take the resume path since reconcile never checks submittable).
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_reconcile_resumes_when_sha_matches`: write a WipChain with tested_shas={"Itip": "sT"}, seed a NEW change_info with revision="sT", call reconcile_recovery, assert `disposition == "resume in-flight stack"` and `(tmp_path / RECOVERY_FILE).exists()`.
